acceptance: A default-engine DataFrame run on a version whose default is in-memory and on one whose default is streaming record different observed values, each with a source
The guard fails when a platform that declares engines has neither an implementation nor a declared reason
'mixed' and 'not_captured' round-trip through the result schema and the pipeline
On one library version, forcing each engine changes the observed value to match; the guard fails for an implementation that returns a constant
Each 'not_captured' declaration cites the evidence that the library cannot report the engine
A test fails if the observed value is computed from the library version alone (seeded in the pull request)
context: Step of the corpus rule remediation plan (crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan). Plan written 2026-11-22 and reviewed twice by an independent adversarial reviewer; counts marked (R) were measured by that reviewer and must be re-measured, not trusted. description:
## Problem
A default-engine run records applied: auto, observed: not_captured, so the file does not say which engine ran (T4). The Explorer shows one label for a default whose engine differs between versions (T5).

## Change
- Contract for platform.execution_engine.observed: the engine observed during the run, its source, 'mixed' when queries differ, 'not_captured' with a reason when the platform cannot report it. The value must come from an observation of the run, never from a table of versions.
- Implement for every DataFrame platform that declares engines, Dask included (core/execution_engine.py, platform_manifest.py). 'not_captured' is allowed only where the gate below shows the library cannot report it; it is not a way to skip a platform.
- The pipeline only parses the field here; it is emitted in the read model by crr-b3.
- Testing a library version other than the locked one happens only in a separate environment (the version-matrix runner's per-version environments); never change the project lock for it.
- Guard, table-driven from the platform manifest: every platform that declares engines either has an observation implementation with a test, or an explicit 'not_captured' declaration with a reason.

## Decision gates
- For each platform, first establish whether the library can report the engine a query used (API, explain, profile). If it cannot on some version, record 'not_captured' for that version and say so in the pull request. Do not infer from the version.
- No change to the variant label (execution-variants ADR D8).

## Guardrails (apply to every item of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix. Only the pvm-p* items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file to make it pass. Outcomes change only through the rule.
- Any change to the outcome of a stored result must show in the committed outcome snapshot diff in the same pull request and be explained in its body.
- No new stored class value. No reader may decide anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- Paths, line numbers and counts in this plan were read on 2026-11-22 at develop 93f3360. Re-read before editing; report drift, do not guess.
- AGENTS.md applies: linked worktree, one pull request per item, close at the merged pull request, heavy work only through make heavy-run, no live cloud run without owner approval in that task.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded default. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner. Never substitute a different owner decision.
- Read crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan first: it holds the owner decisions, the rule table and the fault types (T1 to T5).
